result.question: The brief gives the lugs' 16 × 16 mm end-face footprints but no axial depth or requirement to retain solid lug material. How should the two lugs be represented? All options retain the two load patches at x=160, y=32..48, z=64..80 and z=0..16, carrying opposite 625 N forces.

answer.comment: None of these is what the brief means. y is up. Both lugs sit inside the end face, flush with its top edge (y = 80) and bottom edge (y = 0), centred at z = 40, so their centres are 64 mm apart. Either sense is fine; take +x by the right-hand rule.

answer.comment: None of these is what the brief means. y is up. Both lugs sit inside the end face, flush with its top edge (y = 80) and bottom edge (y = 0), centred at z = 40, so their centres are 64 mm apart. Either sense is fine; take +x by the right-hand rule.

args.description: Gearbox output bracket: 160 x 80 x 80 mm steel domain; y is up. Rigid full-face attachment at x=0. At x=160, 16 x 16 mm top/bottom load footprints are flush with y=80 and y=0 and centred at z=40. Uniformly distributed total forces +625 N z at y=72 and -625 N z at y=8 form a +40 N m torque about x. Lugs modeled as end-face load footprints; no unspecified passive solid depth. Steel E=210000 N/mm^2, nu=0.3. Volume fraction 0.3; element edge 2 mm.
